clue.text: Philosopher superior to a religious community in Devon

parts.note: Isaac Newton, the great natural philosopher
the head of a monastery is its abbot

explanation.surface: A thinker is ranked above a group of monks somewhere in the West Country.
explanation.walkthrough: NEWTON ABBOT is a market town in Devon, a county in south-west England; the definition is just the location phrase, read as 'a place in Devon'.
explanation.definitionFit: The town lies in the English county of Devon, so 'in Devon' points to a place there.

clue.text: Pasta by name and lots of it

parts.note: oodles is informal for lots, a great quantity

explanation.surface: A dish of pasta, labelled by name, served in generous quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: Long thin strips of dough are a kind of pasta.

clue.text: Way to conduct oneself in front of musicians

definitions.text: Way to conduct oneself in front of musicians

parts.words: Way to conduct oneself in front of musicians
parts.note: reads like advice on behaving well before a band, but describes literally conducting them with the stick in hand

explanation.definitionFit: A conductor directs an orchestra by brandishing the stick, so this is the way to conduct before musicians; figuratively it also means taking charge.

clue.text: Don is apparently a singular member of society

parts.note: singular in the sense of strange or peculiar, odd
a university don is a fellow of a college

explanation.surface: A university teacher is, it seems, a rather peculiar member of the community.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oddfellows are a friendly society, a British mutual-aid organisation; one of its members is an Oddfellow. The charade is built in answer order, with 'singular' first.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oddfellow belongs to the friendly society of that name, so is a member of a society.

clue.text: A fish in a jelly may be doubled up

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A fish set in aspic might be served in a doubled portion.
explanation.walkthrough: The jelly from seaweed is often called by its name said twice, agar-agar, which is why it 'may be doubled up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar is a gelatinous substance from seaweed, also known by the reduplicated name.

clue.text: Animal a president gets with a dollar

parts.note: George Bush, a US president
a buck is slang for a dollar

explanation.surface: A head of state comes away with a single dollar.
explanation.definitionFit: The bushbuck is a species of African antelope.

clue.text: Care about right fashion

indicators.note: the word for caring goes about, around, the letter for right

parts.note: to care for is to tend

explanation.surface: Someone worries about whether they are dressed in the correct style.
explanation.definitionFit: A trend is a prevailing fashion or vogue.

clue.text: Their language is Armoric not Serb, anyhow

indicators.note: anyhow means in any old way, so the letters of the two words are thrown into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone insists a language belongs not to Serbs but to another people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyhow' rearranges the letters of NOT SERB. Armoric is an old name for Breton, the Celtic language of Brittany.
explanation.definitionFit: The people of Brittany speak a Celtic tongue once called Armoric, so it is their language.

clue.text: French department and Rene's place

indicators.note: to place is to arrange or set out, so these letters are set in a new order

parts.note: the name Rene with its S kept as a letter

explanation.surface: A region of France is where a man called Rene lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'place' looks like a noun completing 'Rene's place', but works as a verb meaning arrange, rearranging AND RENES.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ardennes is an administrative department in north-east France, on the Belgian border.

clue.text: Artist taking too much out of himself dips into the red?

definitions.text: Artist taking too much out of himself
definitions.meaning: an artist who sketches excessively, drawing too much, exhausting his account
takes more money from a bank account than it holds, so the balance goes negative

explanation.definitionFit: To overdraw is to withdraw more than is in the account; an artist who draws too much literally over-draws.

clue.text: Look around Rhode Island for an inaccessible place

indicators.note: the looking word goes around the state abbreviation

parts.note: to look at something is to eye it
RI is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Rhode Island

explanation.surface: A visitor peers around Rhode Island hunting for a remote spot.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle's nest high on a crag is proverbially hard to reach, so it stands for any lofty remote spot.

clue.text: Did some spooning in a big way

definitions.text: Did some spooning in a big way

parts.words: Did some spooning in a big way
parts.note: spooning suggests courting couples, but it means serving with a large spoon, a big serving spoon

explanation.definitionFit: To serve soup with a large long-handled spoon is to scoop it out in a big way.

clue.text: One badge fashioned for a fiery companion of Daniel

indicators.note: fashioned means shaped or made, so the letters are formed into something new

explanation.surface: A single badge is made for a friend of a biblical prophet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashioned' rearranges ONE BADGE. In the Book of Daniel, Abednego, with Shadrach and Meshach, was thrown into the fiery furnace and survived.
explanation.definitionFit: He was one of Daniel's three friends cast into Nebuchadnezzar's furnace, hence fiery.

clue.text: Pay off old scores, perhaps

parts.note: can mean clearing debts that have run up, or taking revenge for old grievances

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to pay what is owed and to get even with someone for past wrongs.

clue.text: See 2
See 13
Your turn to deliver

parts.note: an invitation to speak next, with a nod to cricket where a bowler delivers a set of six balls

explanation.definitionFit: Handing the floor to someone tells them it is their turn; in cricket a bowler delivers an over.

clue.text: One from a sullen sort of race with an ugly expression

definitions.note: describes the person, a noun, who pulls faces

parts.note: sullen and grim both describe a forbidding look

indicators.note: a sort of race is the word made into a different form, rearranged

explanation.surface: A member of a gloomy-looking people who pulls ugly faces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges RACE into ACER. 'One from' introduces the person; the definition points to someone making an ugly face.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who pulls a contorted face, scowling or wincing, wears an ugly expression.

clue.text: Worrying job for the guitar-maker?

parts.note: a stressful task for a luthier, or the job of fitting frets, the ridges on a guitar neck, worrying being fretting

explanation.definitionFit: Ornamental cut woodwork shares its name with work on the frets of a guitar; to fret is to worry.

clue.text: An accessory healthy chaps take time to put on

parts.note: fit means in good health
chaps are men

explanation.surface: Fit men take a moment to put on an extra item.
explanation.definitionFit: A fitment is a fixed piece of furniture or an attachment, an accessory fitted to something.

clue.text: She's part of the entertainment George is having

definitions.text: She's part of the entertainment George is having

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a section of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A Japanese hostess is among the attractions laid on at George's party.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of George, all of is, and the start of having; the whole clue also describes her.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese hostess trained in music and dance provides entertainment.

clue.text: His citation is not without charge

definitions.text: His citation is not without charge

parts.words: His citation is not without charge
parts.note: reads as a fee for a reference, but means a man who cites someone and lays a charge against them

explanation.definitionFit: One who brings a charge, citing someone in court, is a prosecutor of the complaint.

clue.text: Eye trouble adapted to a march

indicators.note: adapted means altered, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A soldier's eye problem has to be accommodated for a parade.
explanation.definitionFit: Trachoma is a contagious eye infection that can cause blindness.

clue.text: On the cards he's the expert as a rule

definitions.text: On the cards he's the expert
definitions.meaning: Edmond ... wrote the standard rules of card games
'according to' him means by the rules, properly

explanation.definitionFit: Edmond Hoyle codified card-game rules, so the phrase 'according to' him means correctly.

clue.text: A cat, I note, can be so small

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
C is a musical note

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a cat can be tiny.
explanation.definitionFit: Atomic scale means minute, as small as atoms.

clue.text: Frenchman the first chap to find her

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for Monsieur
Adam was the first man in Genesis

explanation.surface: A Frenchman and the original man go looking for a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Madam is a polite address to a woman, standing in for 'her'.

clue.text: Novel midshipman free from pain

definitions.meaning: Mr Midshipman ... is a Captain Marryat sea novel

explanation.definitionFit: Marryat's naval novel names its young hero this; the word also means comfortable.

clue.text: Chopped by one, maybe, but it's hard

indicators.note: chopped means cut up, so the letters are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: Wood split by one person, perhaps, though it is tough going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chopped' rearranges BY ONE; wood being chopped fits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebony is a dense, heavy black timber noted for its hardness.

clue.text: Cautious about bids from Scylla's opposite number

parts.note: chary means wary, cautious

indicators.note: about here means in a jumbled order, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A careful bidder at auction is wary of offers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but rearranges BIDS. In Greek myth Scylla and Charybdis were two sea monsters on opposite sides of a strait.
explanation.definitionFit: The whirlpool monster faced Scylla across the Strait of Messina in Homer's Odyssey.

clue.text: Perhaps it brings out the adder before time

definitions.text: Perhaps it brings out the adder before time

parts.words: Perhaps it brings out the adder before time
parts.note: snakes emerge as the weather warms, but an adder is also one who adds, a summer, placed after early

explanation.definitionFit: Warm weather at the season's start draws snakes into the open; also an adder is one who sums, preceded by a word for before time.
